blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{1}^{2} (x^2 + x)\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Sab se pehle dekhte hain ke sawal kis qisam ka hai: yeh ek seedha definite integral hai, aur integrand ek polynomial hai.
Diya kya hai? \(x^2 + x\) aur limits 1 se 2.
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value, yani ek number (koi \(+c\) nahi).
Rule kaunsa? Har term par power rule laga kar antiderivative \(F(x)\) banayenge, phir Second Fundamental Theorem: upar wali limit ki value minus neeche wali limit ki value.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{1}^{2} (x^2 + x)\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: power rule \(\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\) har term par alag alag, phir Theorem 3.3 (Second FTC) \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a)\). Yeh tareeqa is liye theek hai ke polynomial ka antiderivative seedha mil jata hai, koi substitution nahi chahiye.

Antiderivative banayein
\[\int (x^2 + x)\,dx = \dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{x^2}{2}\]
Kyun: power rule mein power ko ek barha dete hain aur nayi power se divide karte hain: \(x^2\) se \(\frac{x^3}{3}\) aur \(x\) se \(\frac{x^2}{2}\). Constant \(c\) yahan nahi likhte, kyunke \(F(b) - F(a)\) mein woh khud cancel ho jata hai.

Limits daalein
\[\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_{1}^{2}\]
\[= \left(\dfrac{8}{3} + 2\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: pehle upar wali limit \(x = 2\) rakhi, phir neeche wali \(x = 1\), aur pehli value mein se doosri minus ki.
Dhyan dein: brackets zaroor lagaiye; poore lower bracket ka minus hota hai, sirf pehli term ka nahi.

Simplify karein
\[= \dfrac{14}{3} - \dfrac{5}{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{28 - 5}{6} = \dfrac{23}{6}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{8}{3} + 2 = \frac{8 + 6}{3} = \frac{14}{3}\) aur \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2 + 3}{6} = \frac{5}{6}\). Phir common denominator 6 le kar \(\frac{14}{3} = \frac{28}{6}\) likha aur minus kiya.

Tasdeeq
\[f(1) = 2,\quad f(2) = 6\]
\[2 < \dfrac{23}{6} \approx 3.83 < 6 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \([1, 2]\) ki lambai 1 hai aur is par integrand 2 se barh kar 6 tak jata hai. Is liye area 2 se zyada aur 6 se kam hona chahiye, aur 3.83 bilkul isi range mein hai. Answer key mein bhi \(\frac{23}{6}\) hi chhapa hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi polynomial ka definite integral hai, bas ab cubic (power 3 wala) hai aur neeche wali limit negative hai.
Diya kya hai? \(4x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x\) aur limits \(-2\) se \(3\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Plan: power rule se antiderivative, phir \(F(3) - F(-2)\). Asal imtihan signs ka hai: \(x = -2\) rakhte waqt har power ka sign dhyan se dekhna hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{-2}^{3} (4x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x)\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: har term par power rule, phir Second FTC \(F(3) - F(-2)\). Polynomial hai, is liye koi aur technique ki zaroorat nahi.

Antiderivative banayein
\[\int (4x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x)\,dx\]
\[= x^4 + x^3 + x^2\]
Kyun: \(4x^3\) ka integral \(4 \cdot \frac{x^4}{4} = x^4\), \(3x^2\) ka \(3 \cdot \frac{x^3}{3} = x^3\), aur \(2x\) ka \(2 \cdot \frac{x^2}{2} = x^2\). Coefficients aur nayi power aapas mein cancel ho gaye, is liye antiderivative bohat saaf aaya.

Upar wali limit par value
\[F(3) = 81 + 27 + 9 = 117\]
Kyun: \(3^4 = 81\), \(3^3 = 27\), \(3^2 = 9\), teeno jama kiye.

Neeche wali limit par value
\[F(-2) = (-2)^4 + (-2)^3 + (-2)^2\]
\[= 16 - 8 + 4 = 12\]
Kyun: negative number ki even power (2, 4) positive hoti hai, aur odd power (3) negative rehti hai. Is liye \((-2)^4 = 16\), \((-2)^3 = -8\), \((-2)^2 = 4\).
Dhyan dein: \((-2)^3\) ko \(+8\) likhna sab se aam ghalti hai; isi ghalti se jawab badal jata hai (neeche kitab ki ghalti dekhiye).

Minus karein
\[\int_{-2}^{3} (4x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x)\,dx\]
\[= 117 - 12 = 105\]
Kyun: Second FTC ke mutabiq upar wali value minus neeche wali value.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^4 + x^3 + x^2)\]
\[= 4x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: antiderivative ka derivative wapas integrand de raha hai, is liye \(F\) sahi hai. Phir \(F(3)\) aur \(F(-2)\) ko ek ek term kar ke dobara dekha; \(117 - 12 = 105\) pakka hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key mein \(89\) chhapa hai, jo ghalat hai; sahi value \(105\) hai. 89 tab aata hai jab koi \((-2)^3 = +8\) le le: phir \(F(-2) = 16 + 8 + 4 = 28\) aur \(117 - 28 = 89\). Lekin odd power par minus qaim rehta hai, \((-2)^3 = -8\), is liye \(F(-2) = 12\) aur jawab \(117 - 12 = 105\).

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein \(\sin^2 x\) ka integral chahiye. Mushkil yeh hai ke \(\sin^2 x\) ka koi seedha formula nahi hota.
Diya kya hai? \(\sin^2 x\) aur limits \(0\) se \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? Half-angle identity se power kam karenge: \(\sin^2 x = \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\). Is ke baad dono terms ke standard integrals maloom hain.
Plan: identity, integrate, limits.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: half-angle identity \(\sin^2 x = \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\) se square khatam karenge, phir \(\int \cos 2x\,dx = \frac{\sin 2x}{2}\) lagayenge, phir Second FTC.

Power kam karein
\[\sin^2 x = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{2}\]
Kyun: yeh identity \(\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x\) se aati hai (isay \(\sin^2 x\) ke liye solve kar lein). Square wali cheez ko seedha integrate nahi kar sakte, lekin \(\cos 2x\) ka integral aasaan hai. Yani humne mushkil cheez ko aasaan cheez mein badal diya.

Integrate karein
\[\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[x - \dfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{2}\) bahar nikal liya; \(\int 1\,dx = x\), aur \(\int \cos 2x\,dx = \frac{\sin 2x}{2}\), kyunke andar 2 hai to us se divide karna parta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{\sin 2x}{2}\) mein 2 se divide bhool jana aam ghalti hai; derivative le kar dekhein to 2 wapas aa jata hai.

Limits daalein
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\sin \pi}{2}\right) - (0 - 0)\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(\sin \pi = 0\) aur \(\sin 0 = 0\), is liye sine wali terms khatam ho gayin aur sirf \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) bacha.

Tasdeeq: Property IV se doosra raasta
\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^2 x\,dx\]
\[2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} 1\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: Property IV mein \(x\) ki jagah \(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\) rakhein to \(\sin^2 x\) ban jata hai \(\cos^2 x\), lekin integral \(I\) wohi rehta hai. Dono shaklein jama karein to \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\) aata hai, jis ka integral \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) hai. Phir \(I = \frac{\pi}{4}\), wohi jawab. Do mukhtalif raaston se ek hi jawab aana pakki tasdeeq hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \frac{1}{1 + \sin x}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh trigonometric fraction hai jis ke neeche \(1 + \sin x\) hai. Is shakal ka koi seedha formula yaad nahi hota.
Diya kya hai? \(\frac{1}{1 + \sin x}\) aur limits \(0\) se \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? Jaise surds mein conjugate se multiply karte hain, yahan upar neeche \(1 - \sin x\) se multiply karenge. Neeche \(\cos^2 x\) banega aur fraction do standard integrals mein toot jayega.
Plan: multiply, split, integrate, limits.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4} \frac{1}{1 + \sin x}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: \(1 - \sin x\) se upar neeche multiply (conjugate jaisa), \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\) ka istemal, phir \(\int \sec^2 x\,dx = \tan x\) aur \(\int \sec x \tan x\,dx = \sec x\).

Upar neeche \(1 - \sin x\) se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{1}{1 + \sin x} = \dfrac{1 - \sin x}{1 - \sin^2 x}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 - \sin x}{\cos^2 x}\]
Kyun: \((1 + \sin x)(1 - \sin x) = 1 - \sin^2 x\) (difference of squares), aur Pythagorean identity se \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\). Upar neeche ek hi cheez se multiply karne se value nahi badalti; aur \([0, \frac{\pi}{4}]\) par \(1 - \sin x\) kabhi zero nahi hota, is liye yeh jaiz hai.

Fraction ko torein
\[= \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x} - \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\cos x}\]
\[= \sec^2 x - \sec x \tan x\]
Kyun: numerator ke do hisse the, is liye do fractions bane. \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\) aur \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\). Ab dono terms aisi hain jin ke integrals hum zabani jaante hain.

Integrate karein
\[\int_{0}^{\pi/4} (\sec^2 x - \sec x \tan x)\,dx\]
\[= \Big[\tan x - \sec x\Big]_{0}^{\pi/4}\]
Kyun: \(\tan x\) ka derivative \(\sec^2 x\) hai aur \(\sec x\) ka derivative \(\sec x \tan x\); integration derivative ka ulta hai.

Limits daalein
\[= (1 - \sqrt{2}) - (0 - 1)\]
\[= 2 - \sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\), \(\sec\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\cos(\pi/4)} = \sqrt{2}\), \(\tan 0 = 0\), \(\sec 0 = 1\).
Dhyan dein: \(-(0 - 1) = +1\) banta hai; yahan minus ka sign ulta karna na bhooliye.

Tasdeeq
\[2 - \sqrt{2} \approx 0.586\]
\[0.46 < 0.586 < 0.79 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \([0, \frac{\pi}{4}]\) ki lambai taqreeban 0.785 hai. Is par integrand 1 se ghat kar \(\frac{1}{1 + 0.707} \approx 0.586\) tak aata hai. Is liye area \(0.586 \times 0.785 \approx 0.46\) se zyada aur \(1 \times 0.785\) se kam hona chahiye; jawab isi range mein hai.

blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein cosine ki odd power (3) hai.
Diya kya hai? \(\cos^3\theta\) aur limits \(0\) se \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? Odd power mein ek \(\cos\theta\) alag kar lete hain, baqi ko sine mein badal dete hain: \(\cos^3\theta = (1 - \sin^2\theta)\cos\theta\). Phir \(u = \sin\theta\) rakhne se seedha polynomial ban jata hai.
Plan: ek cosine alag, substitution, limits badalna, integrate.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^3\theta\,d\theta\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: definite integral mein substitution: \(u = \sin\theta\), \(du = \cos\theta\,d\theta\), aur limits bhi \(u\) ke hisaab se badlenge. Yeh tareeqa is liye chalta hai ke \(\sin\theta\) ka derivative \(\cos\theta\) integrand mein mojood hai.

Ek cosine alag karein
\[\cos^3\theta = \cos^2\theta \cdot \cos\theta\]
\[= (1 - \sin^2\theta)\cos\theta\]
Kyun: \(\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta\) (Pythagorean identity). Jo ek \(\cos\theta\) bacha, woh \(d\theta\) ke saath mil kar \(du\) banega. Yani humne integrand ko \(u\) aur \(du\) ki zabaan mein likhne ki tayyari kar li.

Substitution aur nayi limits
\[u = \sin\theta,\quad du = \cos\theta\,d\theta\]
\[\theta = 0 \Rightarrow u = 0,\quad \theta = \tfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow u = 1\]
\[\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^3\theta\,d\theta = \int_{0}^{1} (1 - u^2)\,du\]
Kyun: definite integral mein substitution karte waqt limits bhi nayi variable ki ho jati hain: \(\sin 0 = 0\) aur \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\). Is ka faida yeh hai ke wapas \(\theta\) mein jane ki zaroorat nahi.
Dhyan dein: purani limits \(0\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ko \(u\) wale integral par lagana bohat aam ghalti hai.

Integrate karein
\[= \left[u - \dfrac{u^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
Kyun: power rule; \(u = 0\) par dono terms zero hain, is liye sirf upar wali value bachi.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{d\theta}\left(\sin\theta - \dfrac{\sin^3\theta}{3}\right)\]
\[= \cos\theta - \sin^2\theta\cos\theta = \cos^3\theta \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\theta\) mein antiderivative ka derivative wapas integrand de raha hai (chain rule se \(\frac{d}{d\theta}\sin^3\theta = 3\sin^2\theta\cos\theta\)). Is par limits lagayein to bhi \(1 - \frac{1}{3}\) hi aata hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (vi) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{\sqrt{x}}{1 + x}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Is integrand mein asal rukawat \(\sqrt{x}\) hai; root ke saath fraction ka seedha formula nahi.
Diya kya hai? \(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{1 + x}\) aur limits \(0\) se \(1\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? \(x = t^2\) rakh denge, to \(\sqrt{x} = t\) ban jayega aur root khatam. Phir rational function bachega jis mein upar aur neeche ki degree barabar hai, to pehle divide karenge.
Plan: substitution, limits badalna, divide, integrate.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{\sqrt{x}}{1 + x}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: substitution \(x = t^2\), \(dx = 2t\,dt\) (root hatane ke liye), phir \(\frac{t^2}{1 + t^2} = 1 - \frac{1}{1 + t^2}\) aur standard integral \(\int \frac{dt}{1 + t^2} = \tan^{-1} t\).

Substitution aur nayi limits
\[x = t^2,\quad dx = 2t\,dt,\quad \sqrt{x} = t\]
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow t = 0,\quad x = 1 \Rightarrow t = 1\]
\[I = \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{t}{1 + t^2} \cdot 2t\,dt\]
\[= 2\int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{t^2}{1 + t^2}\,dt\]
Kyun: \(x = t^2\) ka differential \(dx = 2t\,dt\) hai. \([0, 1]\) par hum \(t = \sqrt{x}\) ko positive lete hain, is liye \(\sqrt{x}\) bilkul \(t\) ban jata hai. Limits: \(x = 0\) par \(t = 0\), \(x = 1\) par \(t = 1\); yahan limits ittefaq se wohi rahin, lekin yeh check karna zaroori tha.

Fraction ko divide karein
\[\dfrac{t^2}{1 + t^2} = \dfrac{(1 + t^2) - 1}{1 + t^2}\]
\[= 1 - \dfrac{1}{1 + t^2}\]
Kyun: upar aur neeche dono ki degree 2 hai. Aisi surat mein pehle 'poora hissa' alag karte hain: numerator mein 1 jama aur 1 minus kiya, to ek poora 1 nikal aaya aur baqi \(\frac{1}{1 + t^2}\) bacha, jis ka integral \(\tan^{-1} t\) hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{t^2}{1 + t^2}\) ko seedha \(\tan^{-1}\) samajh lena ghalat hai; pehle divide zaroori hai.

Integrate karein
\[I = 2\Big[t - \tan^{-1} t\Big]_{0}^{1}\]
\[= 2\left(1 - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - 0\]
\[= 2 - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\tan^{-1} 1 = \frac{\pi}{4}\) (kyunke \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\)) aur \(\tan^{-1} 0 = 0\).

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{2} \leq \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 + x} \leq \sqrt{x}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{3} < 2 - \dfrac{\pi}{2} \approx 0.429 < \dfrac{2}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \([0, 1]\) par \(1 + x\) ki value 1 aur 2 ke darmiyan hai, is liye integrand \(\frac{\sqrt{x}}{2}\) aur \(\sqrt{x}\) ke darmiyan rehta hai. \(\int_0^1 \sqrt{x}\,dx = \frac{2}{3}\) hai, to Property VIII ke mutabiq jawab \(\frac{1}{3}\) aur \(\frac{2}{3}\) ke beech hona chahiye; 0.429 beech mein hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (vii) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{\ln(1 + x)}{1 + x^2}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh is exercise ka mushkil sawal hai: \(\frac{\ln(1 + x)}{1 + x^2}\) ka koi seedha antiderivative nahi milta, is liye aam tareeqe se integral nahi hoga.
Diya kya hai? Limits \(0\) se \(1\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? Neeche \(1 + x^2\) dekh kar \(x = \tan\theta\) ka khayal aata hai. Phir Property IV lagayenge (\(\theta\) ki jagah \(\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta\)); integral dobara khud ki shakal mein wapas aa jayega, aur ek equation se \(I\) nikal lenge.
Plan: \(x = \tan\theta\), Property IV, log ke rules, equation solve.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(I = \int_{0}^{1} \frac{\ln(1 + x)}{1 + x^2}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: \(I\).
Tareeqa: substitution \(x = \tan\theta\), phir Property IV \(\int_a^b f(\theta)\,d\theta = \int_a^b f(a + b - \theta)\,d\theta\), aur identity \(\tan(\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta) = \frac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}\). Is qisam ke integrals mein antiderivative dhoondne ke bajaye integral ko khud se jor kar equation banate hain.

\(x = \tan\theta\) rakhein
\[dx = \sec^2\theta\,d\theta,\quad 1 + x^2 = \sec^2\theta\]
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow \theta = 0,\quad x = 1 \Rightarrow \theta = \tfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \ln(1 + \tan\theta)\,d\theta\]
Kyun: \(1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta\), aur \(dx\) mein bhi \(\sec^2\theta\) aata hai, to dono cancel ho gaye. Limits: \(\tan 0 = 0\) aur \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\). Ab integrand bohat saada ho gaya.

Property IV lagayein
\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \ln\left(1 + \tan\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4} - \theta\right)\right)d\theta\]
Kyun: yahan \(a + b = 0 + \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4}\), is liye \(\theta\) ki jagah \(\frac{\pi}{4} - \theta\) rakh sakte hain; integral ki value nahi badalti, kyunke yeh sirf interval ko ulti taraf se parhna hai.

Bracket ko simplify karein
\[1 + \dfrac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta} = \dfrac{2}{1 + \tan\theta}\]
\[\ln\dfrac{2}{1 + \tan\theta} = \ln 2 - \ln(1 + \tan\theta)\]
Kyun: \(\tan(A - B)\) ke formula mein \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\) rakha to \(\frac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}\) mila. Is mein 1 jama kiya: \(\frac{(1 + \tan\theta) + (1 - \tan\theta)}{1 + \tan\theta} = \frac{2}{1 + \tan\theta}\). Phir log ka qanoon \(\ln\frac{p}{q} = \ln p - \ln q\).

Integral dobara saamne aa gaya
\[I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \ln 2\,d\theta - I\]
\[2I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\ln 2\]
\[I = \dfrac{\pi}{8}\ln 2\]
Kyun: doosra hissa bilkul wohi asal integral \(I\) hai. \(\ln 2\) ek constant hai, us ka integral \(\frac{\pi}{4} \cdot \ln 2\) (constant times interval ki lambai). \(I\) ko left side le gaye aur 2 se divide kiya.
Dhyan dein: yahan \(I\) ko 'unknown' samajh kar equation ki tarah solve karna hai; antiderivative ki talaash mein waqt zaya na karein.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{\pi}{8}\ln 2 \approx 0.2722\]
Kyun: \(x = 0\) par integrand 0 hai aur \(x = 1\) par \(\frac{\ln 2}{2} \approx 0.35\). Lambai 1 hai, to area 0 aur 0.35 ke darmiyan hona chahiye. Calculator se numerical value 0.27220 aati hai, jo bilkul hamare jawab ke barabar hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (viii) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{0}^{1} \tan^{-1} x\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Is integral mein sirf ek inverse function \(\tan^{-1} x\) hai, aur us ka koi seedha formula yaad nahi hota.
Diya kya hai? Limits \(0\) se \(1\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? Integration by parts: \(\tan^{-1} x\) ko pehla function aur \(1\) ko doosra function maan lete hain. Is ka faida yeh hai ke \(\tan^{-1} x\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{1 + x^2}\) ek aasaan algebraic cheez hai.
Plan: by parts ka definite form, phir dono hisse alag alag.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int_{0}^{1} \tan^{-1} x\,dx\).
Maloom karna: is ki value.
Tareeqa: definite integrals ke liye integration by parts \(\int_a^b f g\,dx = \left[f \int g\,dx\right]_a^b - \int_a^b \left(\int g\,dx\right) f'\,dx\), jahan \(f = \tan^{-1} x\) aur \(g = 1\). Jab akela log ya inverse trig function ho to yahi '1 se multiply' wala tareeqa kaam aata hai.

By parts lagayein
\[\int_{0}^{1} \tan^{-1} x \cdot 1\,dx\]
\[= \Big[x\tan^{-1} x\Big]_{0}^{1} - \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{x}{1 + x^2}\,dx\]
Kyun: doosre function \(1\) ka integral \(x\) hai, aur pehle function \(\tan^{-1} x\) ka derivative \(\frac{1}{1 + x^2}\). Formula mein rakhne se \(x \cdot \frac{1}{1 + x^2}\) wala naya integral bana, jo pehle se aasaan hai.

Pehla hissa
\[\Big[x\tan^{-1} x\Big]_{0}^{1} = 1 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{4} - 0 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Kyun: \(\tan^{-1} 1 = \frac{\pi}{4}\), aur \(x = 0\) par poori term zero hai.

Doosra hissa
\[\int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{x}{1 + x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\Big[\ln(1 + x^2)\Big]_{0}^{1}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}(\ln 2 - \ln 1) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln 2\]
Kyun: \(1 + x^2\) ka derivative \(2x\) hai; upar sirf \(x\) hai, yani derivative ka aadha. Is liye \(\int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln f(x)\) wala rule \(\frac{1}{2}\) ke saath lagta hai. \(\ln 1 = 0\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{2}\) bhool jana aam ghalti hai; derivative le kar check karein.

Dono ko milayein
\[\int_{0}^{1} \tan^{-1} x\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln 2\]
Kyun: by parts ke formula mein pehla hissa minus doosra hissa.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln 2 \approx 0.439\]
\[\dfrac{\pi}{8} \approx 0.393 < 0.439 < \dfrac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.785 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \([0, 1]\) par \(\tan^{-1} x\) hamesha \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) se neeche hai, aur us seedhi line \(\frac{\pi}{4}x\) se upar hai jo \((0, 0)\) aur \((1, \frac{\pi}{4})\) ko jorti hai (kyunke graph neeche ki taraf mura hua hai). Us line ke neeche ka area \(\frac{\pi}{8}\) hai. Jawab in dono ke beech hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ix) Evaluate the following definite integral: \(\int_{0}^{2\pi} \frac{\sin^2 x}{1 + e^{\cos x}}\,dx\)
blocks.explanation:
Is integrand mein \(e^{\cos x}\) neeche hai; is ka antiderivative dhoondna bekaar hai. Aise sawal properties se hal hote hain.
Diya kya hai? \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{1 + e^{\cos x}}\) aur limits \(0\) se \(2\pi\).
Find kya karna hai? Integral ki value.
Rule kaunsa? Pehle Property VI se interval aadha (\([0, \pi]\)) karenge. Phir Property IV se \(\cos x\) ko \(-\cos x\) mein badlenge, aur dono shaklon ko jama karenge; Example 54 wali identity \(\frac{1}{1 + e^{u}} + \frac{1}{1 + e^{-u}} = 1\) sab saaf kar degi.
Plan: aadha interval, Property IV, jama, \(\int \sin^2 x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(I = \int_{0}^{2\pi} \frac{\sin^2 x}{1 + e^{\cos x}}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: \(I\).
Tareeqa: Property VI: agar \(f(a - x) = f(x)\) ho to \(\int_0^{a} f(x)\,dx = 2\int_0^{a/2} f(x)\,dx\). Phir Property IV aur identity \(\frac{1}{1 + e^{u}} + \frac{1}{1 + e^{-u}} = 1\).

Interval aadha karein (Property VI, \(a = 2\pi\))
\[\sin^2(2\pi - x) = \sin^2 x,\quad \cos(2\pi - x) = \cos x\]
\[I = 2\int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{1 + e^{\cos x}}\,dx = 2J\]
Kyun: \(x\) ki jagah \(2\pi - x\) rakhne se integrand bilkul wohi rehta hai: \(\sin(2\pi - x) = -\sin x\) magar square se minus khatam, aur \(\cos(2\pi - x) = \cos x\). Is ka matlab hai ke \([0, \pi]\) aur \([\pi, 2\pi]\) dono aadhon ka integral barabar hai. Naye integral ko hum \(J\) keh lete hain.

\([0, \pi]\) par Property IV
\[\sin(\pi - x) = \sin x,\quad \cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\]
\[J = \int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{1 + e^{-\cos x}}\,dx\]
Kyun: yahan \(a + b = \pi\), is liye \(x\) ki jagah \(\pi - x\) rakha. \(\sin^2\) wohi raha lekin exponent mein \(\cos x\) ka sign ulat gaya. \(J\) ki value wohi hai, bas shakal nayi hai.

\(J\) ki dono shaklein jama karein
\[2J = \int_{0}^{\pi} \sin^2 x\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + e^{\cos x}} + \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{-\cos x}}\right)dx\]
\[\dfrac{1}{1 + e^{u}} + \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{-u}} = \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{u}} + \dfrac{e^{u}}{e^{u} + 1} = 1\]
Kyun: doosre fraction ke upar neeche \(e^{u}\) se multiply kiya to \(\frac{e^{u}}{e^{u} + 1}\) bana; ab dono ka denominator ek hai aur numerators ka jama \(1 + e^{u}\), yani poora 1. Yahan \(u = \cos x\). Mushkil hissa poora ka poora ghaib ho gaya.

Hisaab mukammal karein
\[2J = \int_{0}^{\pi} \sin^2 x\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
\[J = \dfrac{\pi}{4},\quad I = 2J = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\int_0^{\pi} \sin^2 x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\left[x - \frac{\sin 2x}{2}\right]_0^{\pi} = \frac{\pi}{2}\), bilkul part (iii) wale tareeqe se. Phir \(J = \frac{\pi}{4}\) aur \(I = 2J\).
Dhyan dein: aakhir mein \(I = 2J\) karna na bhooliye; \(J\) sirf aadhe interval ka integral hai.

Tasdeeq
\[I = \dfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{2\pi} \sin^2 x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \pi\]
Kyun: do weights \(\frac{1}{1 + e^{\cos x}}\) aur \(\frac{1}{1 + e^{-\cos x}}\) ka jama hamesha 1 hai, to average weight \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai; is liye jawab \(\sin^2 x\) ke poore integral \(\pi\) ka aadha hona chahiye. Calculator se numerical value 1.570796 aati hai, jo \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) hi hai.
